title: research_report
description: A research report. Every finding carries the three mandatory sections: OBSERVATION (what a cited source shows), HYPOTHESIS (what we infer) and RECOMMENDATION (what we propose, with a confidence). Structure is enforced here; the counting rule 'a recommendation marked high confidence needs at least three sources on three different domains' needs the source table to resolve ids and is for the reviewer to check against the source table.

task_ref.description: The research task this report answers, e.g. T1-03.

question.description: The question the report set out to answer.

sources.description: Every source consulted, with its retrieval date. Keep the same table in docs/research/sources.yaml when the project tracks sources across reports.

gaps.description: Questions the available sources could not answer. Stating a gap is preferred over filling it with a guess.

second_opinion.description: A synthesis of the same corpus by the other vendor lane, attached to reduce single-vendor bias.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 with an explicit offset, as supervisor.store.now_iso() writes it. The pattern is carried next to 'format' on purpose: no RFC-3339 format checker is installed, so without it the format keyword would be annotation only.

observation.description: OBSERVATION: only what the cited sources show. An anecdote is allowed here but can never be the sole support of a recommendation.

hypothesis.description: HYPOTHESIS: the inference drawn from the observation, stated so it could be wrong.

recommendation.description: RECOMMENDATION: what we propose. 'high' confidence requires at least three sources on three distinct domains (reviewers check this against the source table).

publisher.description: Publishing domain or organisation; independence is judged on this.

published.description: Publication date as the source states it; prefer recent, dated sources.
